about: Gold set for SkillRet: does skill retrieval surface the right card for a
real opening message?
Rules this file is written under, because breaking them silently inflates
every number downstream:
1. Queries are in a USER's voice, not the author's. An echoing query -- one
that reuses the words of the brief it is meant to find -- scores 20-40
points higher than a real one, so a corpus tested that way looks fine
right up until someone uses it. Where a query names a real symbol
($mutex, verb_code, objdef) that is because a user would name it too.
2. Relevance is graded, and a PARENT of a gold child scores 1, not 0.
Parent absorption is deliberate: the ranker collapses a parent and its
own children into the parent, whose card indexes the children, so the
agent descends on its own. Scoring that as a miss would penalise the
design rather than measure it. A child returned in its own right scores
2 because it saves a fetch.
3. No negative cases with empty gold. The ranker returns `limit` cards
whatever is asked, so 'should return nothing' is not a behaviour it can
exhibit, and grading it would only add noise.
4. The near-miss pairs are the point. moor/* (the Rust engine) against
thetis-internals/* (this agent's own machinery) is the confusion this
corpus is actually prone to, and several cases below exist only to
check that the two do not bleed into each other.
5. Every gold id must exist in the pinned corpus (corpus/v1). Cases that
referenced skills/torchship were removed: that subtree is deliberately
not pushed to the remote, so those cases were only scoreable on one
checkout and reported as unwinnable everywhere else. A gold id absent
from the corpus makes a case impossible to win and silently drags the
mean down, which is why run.sh warns about unknown ids.
